items.name: Weekly store-item demand forecast
items.statement: Set next week's replenishment quantity for each item in each store. Fewer stock-outs and less excess stock on the highest-volume channel.

items.name: Warehouse reorder points from on-hand stock
items.statement: Set the reorder point and order quantity per item and warehouse. Avoids stock-outs and cuts the cash tied up in slow stock.

items.name: Return rate by item and reason
items.statement: Fix, delist or relabel the items with the highest return rates and their main return reasons. Returns erase margin; the top reasons point to quality or description fixes.

items.name: Suspicious return behavior per customer
items.statement: Flag customers or tickets whose return pattern looks abusive for review before refunding. Return abuse is a direct and recurring loss.

items.name: Customer lapse risk from purchase recency and frequency
items.statement: Choose which customers get a win-back offer this week. Retaining existing customers costs less than acquiring new ones.

items.name: Customer lifetime value across channels
items.statement: Set the service level and marketing budget per customer tier. Spending follows value; channel-blind value hides the best customers.

items.name: Customer segments from demographics and spend
items.statement: Pick the segments to target with each campaign. Targeted campaigns convert better than broadcast ones.

items.name: Promotion effectiveness by channel
items.statement: Keep, change or stop each promotion based on incremental sales against its cost. Promotion spend that does not lift sales is pure margin loss.

items.name: Price elasticity and markdown depth
items.statement: Set the markdown depth per item category. Too-deep markdowns give away margin; too-shallow ones leave stock unsold.

items.name: Cross-channel cannibalization
items.statement: Decide channel-specific assortment and pricing where one channel takes sales from another. Channel conflict can grow costs without growing total sales.

items.name: Market basket affinity for cross-sell
items.statement: Choose product pairs for placement and bundles. Bundles and adjacency lift basket size.

items.name: Store productivity benchmarking
items.statement: Target the stores below their peers on sales per square foot and per employee. Peer benchmarks expose fixable underperformance.

items.name: Shipping cost by ship mode and carrier
items.statement: Renegotiate or switch carriers and ship modes with the worst cost per order. Shipping is a large and negotiable cost line.

items.name: Order-to-ship lag by warehouse
items.statement: Fix the warehouses and ship modes with the longest order-to-ship lag. Slow fulfillment drives cancellations and returns.

items.name: Call center return handling
items.statement: Coach or staff the call centers with the highest return amounts. Return handling quality varies by center and costs money.

items.name: Catalog page effectiveness
items.statement: Drop or redesign the catalog pages that sell least for their department. Print pages have a fixed cost each and should earn it.

items.name: Web page content and sales
items.statement: Change the page types and content that underperform on sales. Page content changes are cheap and testable.

items.name: Margin by brand and category
items.statement: Rationalize the assortment: drop or reprice low-margin brands. Shelf space should go to the products that earn margin.

items.name: Staffing by hour from sales by time of day
items.statement: Set store staffing per shift from expected traffic. Labor is the largest controllable store cost.

items.name: Holiday and seasonal demand planning
items.statement: Set holiday-period orders and staffing per category. Peak periods carry a large share of yearly sales.

items.name: Store site selection from customer geography
items.statement: Choose the regions for the next store openings. Opening near demand that is underserved today grows sales.

items.name: Purchasing power by income band
items.statement: Set the price tiers and assortment per income band. Matching price tiers to buying power lifts conversion.

items.name: Coupon and discount leakage
items.statement: Tighten coupon rules where discounts exceed their intended share of sales. Discount leakage erodes margin quietly.

items.name: Inventory balancing across warehouses
items.statement: Move stock between warehouses to match demand. Rebalancing cuts both stock-outs and overstock.

items.name: Refund method cost on returns
items.statement: Steer refunds toward store credit where it cuts net loss. Store credit keeps revenue that a cash refund loses.
